title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: package ships illness_death, simulated event history data 150 individuals risk illness z, can occur , death. illness raises hazard death, hazards depend baseline covariate L0. Follow-subject censoring. data long format one row per event columns: id: individual identifier. time: event time. event: name process jumped, "z", "death" "censoring". Baseline covariates, L0. format simevent::simulate_events() returns, simulated data can passed straight fit_initial(). individual dies without falling ill single row, one falls ill later dies two rows. example, individual 3 dies, individual 4 falls ill dies:

what: Step 1: Fit the initial hazard models
title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: fit_initial() fits one hazard model per event process, expands data grid observed event times horizon tau, builds discrete state space targeting step works . process gets formula models, process name left covariates hazard right. processes can used covariates name, giving number events far: death hazard depends whether individual fallen ill (z). illness can occur , hazard_model() expresses limit = 1. Every event data needs model, including censoring. type process inferred data: death censoring end follow-, illness occurs . default hazards fitted Cox models. hazard_model() can also restrict individuals risk condition processes, at_risk = ~ z == 0, fit = "hal" uses highly adaptive lasso instead (experimental).
code: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1 ) fit #> Initial fit of 150 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type          model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>         <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z one_jump         z ~ L0    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ L0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal censoring ~ L0   FALSE

what: Step 2: Estimate under a fixed intervention
title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: tmle_estimate() estimates target parameter intervention. target given risk(), risk death time tau. Without intervention, observed risk death time 1: printed table gives targeted estimate standard error 95% confidence interval, stored observed$estimate. intervention scale_intensity(z = 0.5) halves intensity illness: coef() confint() extract estimate confidence intervals levels: factor 0 removes illness altogether, factor 1 increases intensity. factor can also vary time, given formula time, baseline covariates processes:
code: observed <- tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death)) observed #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> without intervention #>  #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3250469 0.03906316 0.2484845 0.4016093 #>  #> Initial estimate: 0.325; converged after 1 iterations halved <- tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), scale_intensity(z = 0.5)) halved #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(z = 0.5) #>  #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3040549 0.03853505 0.2285276 0.3795823 #>  #> Initial estimate: 0.3124; converged after 2 iterations coef(halved) #>     death  #> 0.3040549 confint(halved, level = 0.9) #>             5 %      95 % #> death 0.2406704 0.3674395 tmle_estimate(   fit,   risk(death),   scale_intensity(z = ~ ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1)) )$estimate #>    target  estimate         se     lower    upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>    <num> #> 1:  death 0.3163871 0.03873481 0.2404683 0.392306

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: calibrate() describes calibrated intervention: scaling exposure’s intensity chosen exposure attains given value, target estimated . value given calibration rule: level(theta): exposure equals theta. absolute_change(delta): exposure delta plus observed value. relative_change(rho): exposure rho times observed value. example, risk death risk illness reduced 80% observed value: first table gives calibrated scaling alpha exposure risk theta attains, second risk death . standard error se accounts alpha estimated, whereas se_crude treats known. target can also expected years life lost tau, years_lost(), exposure still calibrated risk:
code: cal <- tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(0.8))) cal #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(0.8)) #>  #>    quantity  estimate         se      lower     upper #>      <char>     <num>      <num>      <num>     <num> #> 1:    alpha 0.7927238 0.00995552 0.77321133 0.8122363 #> 2:    theta 0.1271303 0.02505712 0.07801922 0.1762413 #>  #> Estimates under the calibrated intervention: #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.3199203 0.03864198 0.2441835 0.3956572 0.03866085 tmle_estimate(   fit,   years_lost(death),   calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(0.8)) )$estimate #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper   se_crude #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num>      <num> #> 1:  death 0.1644942 0.02295448 0.1195042 0.2094842 0.02295436

title: Getting started with MultiStateTMLE
text: baseline treatment A0, total effect treatment outcome can split part goes effect exposure remainder. calibrated intervention sets treated individuals’ exposure risk placebo, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total effect : mediated contrast: treatment versus calibrated intervention, calibrated contrast: calibrated intervention versus placebo. illness_death treatment, illustration add randomised treatment actual effect. treatment model given treatment_model, fit_initial() prepares estimates treatment values, = 0 = 1. contrasts computed influence curves fit returns. calibrated arm set = 1 calibrate relative change 1 risk illness placebo, reference_a = 0, risk illness treatment calibrated equal placebo: treatment randomised without effect, confidence intervals three contrasts cover zero, expected.
code: set.seed(1) treated <- illness_death a0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5) treated$A0 <- a0[treated$id]  fit_treated <- fit_initial(   treated,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0 + A0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + A0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = A0 ~ L0 ) treatment_fit <- tmle_estimate(fit_treated, risk(death), a = 1) placebo_fit <- tmle_estimate(fit_treated, risk(death), a = 0) calibrated_fit <- tmle_estimate(   fit_treated,   risk(death),   calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(1), reference_a = 0),   a = 1 )  calibrated_contrasts(treatment_fit, placebo_fit, calibrated_fit) #> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts #>  #>    target   contrast   estimate         se       lower      upper #>    <char>     <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>      <num> #> 1:  death      total -0.1405813 0.07724416 -0.29197704 0.01081449 #> 2:  death   mediated -0.0234265 0.01632300 -0.05541899 0.00856599 #> 3:  death calibrated -0.1171548 0.08141345 -0.27672220 0.04241266

title: Causal Inference for Multistate Event Processes via TMLE
text: pipeline three main steps: fit_initial() fits initial (nuisance) hazard models event process data, builds discrete product state space used internally. tmle_estimate() targets initial fit estimate target, risk(death), stochastic intensity intervention: fixed scaling intensity process, scale_intensity(z = 0.5), one calibrated bring exposure given value, calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(0.8)) (optionally combined intervention baseline treatment). returns TMLE estimate standard error efficient influence curve. intervention_curve() traces target responds exposure grid scalings, calibrated_contrasts() decomposes total treatment effect mediated calibrated contrasts. example, simulated illness-death data illness_death, illness z raises risk death, risk death time 1 intensity illness halved estimated : simulate multistate event history data, see simevent package, whose output fit_initial() takes .
code: library(MultiStateTMLE) fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1 )  tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), scale_intensity(z = 0.5)) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(z = 0.5) #> #>    target  estimate         se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>      <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3040549 0.03853505 0.2285276 0.3795823 #> #> Initial estimate: 0.3124; converged after 2 iterations

title: Decompose a treatment effect into mediated and calibrated contrasts — calibrated_contrasts
text: object class calibrated_contrasts, list elements: estimate: data.table one row per contrast (total, mediated calibrated) columns target, contrast, estimate, se, lower upper. target level: target confidence level. checks: list decomposition_error eic_decomposition_error, far estimates influence curves satisfying total = mediated + calibrated, zero numerical error.

title: Decompose a treatment effect into mediated and calibrated contrasts — calibrated_contrasts
code: # illness_death with a randomised treatment A0 added, for illustration. set.seed(1) treated <- illness_death treated$A0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5)[treated$id]  fit <- fit_initial(   treated,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0 + A0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + A0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = A0 ~ L0 )  # \donttest{ # How much of the effect of treatment on death goes through its effect on # the risk of z? The calibrated intervention gives the treated the risk of z # they would have had under placebo (reference_a = 0): contrasts <- calibrated_contrasts(   treatment_fit = tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), a = 1),   placebo_fit = tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), a = 0),   calibrated_fit = tmle_estimate(     fit,     risk(death),     calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(1), reference_a = 0),     a = 1   ) ) contrasts #> Decomposition of the effect of a on death into mediated and calibrated contrasts #>  #>    target   contrast   estimate         se       lower      upper #>    <char>     <char>      <num>      <num>       <num>      <num> #> 1:  death      total -0.1405813 0.07724416 -0.29197704 0.01081449 #> 2:  death   mediated -0.0234265 0.01632300 -0.05541899 0.00856599 #> 3:  death calibrated -0.1171548 0.08141345 -0.27672220 0.04241266  # The total effect is the sum of the mediated and calibrated contrasts: sum(contrasts$estimate$estimate[2:3]) - contrasts$estimate$estimate[1] #> [1] 0 # }

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
text: data data.frame observed event history data long format, one row per event columns id, time event (name process jumped), plus baseline covariates used models. format simevent::simulate_events(). models list hazard model event process: formula death ~ L0 + z, naming process left covariates right, hazard_model() also restrict individuals risk . processes can used covariates name, giving number events far. Every event data needs model, including censoring process. tau Positive number. Follow-horizon; target parameters evaluated tau. censoring String. Name censoring process models. treatment_model Optional logistic regression model baseline treatment, two-sided formula A0 ~ L0. Required arms given. arms Integer vector baseline treatment values (0/1) prepare interventional hazards clever weights . value can passed tmle_estimate() intervention_curve(). Defaults values, 0:1, treatment_model given. max_count Positive integer. Maximum number jumps tracked per recurrent process state space. depend_time Experimental, may change. Named list one-sided formulas time, making hazards depend time jump. named state variable: process z jumps , z.k kth jump recurrent process z. adds covariate T.<name>, 0 jump formula evaluated time jump , can used (factor) models. example, list(z = ~ time > 0.5) distinguishes early late jumps. control named list tuning settings: prune_states (FALSE): TRUE, prune states admissible -risk conditions models. use_exponential (FALSE): TRUE, always transform hazard increments dH probabilities 1 - exp(-dH). Otherwise done increments exceed 1. hal_control named list settings processes fitted fit = "hal", see Details. cores Positive integer. Number cores used parallel::mclapply() predicting hazards across states. verbose Logical. TRUE, print model fits progress.

Columns data named process, event counts simevent::simulate_events() adds, ignored: counts recomputed event.

title: Fit the initial hazard models — fit_initial
code: # Illness-death data: z is an illness that can occur once, death ends # follow-up, and so does censoring. One row per event: head(illness_death) #>   id      time event         L0 #> 1  1 1.0836890 death  0.2724785 #> 2  2 0.6539194 death  0.3572619 #> 3  3 0.1212156 death -0.8616620 #> 4  4 1.1416233     z  0.8083350 #> 5  4 3.6778032 death  0.8083350 #> 6  5 1.0962284     z  0.6127352  # One hazard model per process. The death hazard depends on whether the # individual has fallen ill, and the illness can occur at most once: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1 ) fit #> Initial fit of 150 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type          model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>         <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z one_jump         z ~ L0    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ L0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal censoring ~ L0   FALSE  # The process types are inferred from the data, and the hazard models are # kept for reference: fit$processes #>         name     type          model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>         <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z one_jump         z ~ L0    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ L0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal censoring ~ L0   FALSE fit$models$death #> Hazard model: death ~ L0 + z  # With a baseline treatment A0, a treatment model prepares estimates under # both arms, for `a` in tmle_estimate(): treated <- illness_death treated$A0 <- rbinom(max(treated$id), 1, 0.5)[treated$id] fit_treated <- fit_initial(   treated,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0 + A0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + A0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1,   treatment_model = A0 ~ L0 ) fit_treated #> Initial fit of 150 individuals up to tau = 1 #>  #>         name     type               model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>              <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z one_jump         z ~ L0 + A0    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ L0 + A0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal      censoring ~ L0   FALSE #>  #> Treatment model: A0 ~ L0, prepared for arms a = 0, 1  # \donttest{ # Data simulated with simevent can be passed as is. Here relapse is # recurrent, and the death hazard grows with the number of relapses so far, # tracked up to max_count: if (requireNamespace("simevent", quietly = TRUE)) {   model <- simevent::sim_model(     L0 = simevent::sim_covariate(function(N) rnorm(N)),     relapse = simevent::sim_process("transient", eta = 0.6, nu = 1),     death = simevent::sim_process("terminal", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     censoring = simevent::sim_process("censoring", eta = 0.2, nu = 1),     effects = list(       simevent::sim_effect(relapse ~ L0, coef = 0.5),       simevent::sim_effect(death ~ relapse, coef = 0.4)     )   )   relapses <- simevent::simulate_events(model, n = 200, seed = 1)    fit_initial(     relapses,     models = list(relapse ~ L0, death ~ L0 + relapse, censoring ~ L0),     tau = 2,     max_count = 3   ) } #> Initial fit of 200 individuals up to tau = 2 #>  #>         name      type                model at_risk #>       <char>    <char>               <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:   relapse recurrent         relapse ~ L0   FALSE #> 2:     death  terminal death ~ L0 + relapse   FALSE #> 3: censoring  terminal       censoring ~ L0   FALSE # }

title: Specify the hazard model of an event process — hazard_model
text: formula two-sided formula. left-hand side names process, matching name event column data, right-hand side gives covariates hazard, survival::coxph() formula. processes can used covariates name, giving number events far. limit Optional positive integer. Maximum number events process per individual: individuals risk fewer limit events. limit = 1 event can happen , sim_process(limit = 1) simevent. at_risk Optional one-sided formula, ~ z == 0, condition processes (number events far). Individuals risk process holds. Combined limit given. fit hazard fitted: "cox" (default), Cox model, "hal", highly adaptive lasso (experimental, see fit_initial()).

title: Specify the hazard model of an event process — hazard_model
code: # A plain formula in fit_initial()'s `models` is short for # hazard_model(formula): hazard_model(death ~ L0 + z) #> Hazard model: death ~ L0 + z  # An illness that can happen at most once: hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1) #> Hazard model: z ~ L0 #>   limit: 1  # A relapse that can happen at most twice, and only before death of # another cause, w: hazard_model(relapse ~ L0, limit = 2, at_risk = ~ w == 0) #> Hazard model: relapse ~ L0 #>   limit: 2 #>   at risk while: w == 0  # Death depending on having had two or more relapses. As in any R model # formula, wrap arithmetic and comparisons in I(): hazard_model(death ~ L0 + I(relapse >= 2)) #> Hazard model: death ~ L0 + I(relapse >= 2)  # Use them in fit_initial(), mixed with plain formulas: fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1 ) fit$processes #>         name     type          model at_risk #>       <char>   <char>         <char>  <lgcl> #> 1:         z one_jump         z ~ L0    TRUE #> 2:     death terminal death ~ L0 + z   FALSE #> 3: censoring terminal censoring ~ L0   FALSE

title: Stochastic intensity interventions — interventions
text: scale_intensity() fixed intensity-scaling intervention: multiplies intensity named process factor alpha, \(\Lambda^z \mapsto \alpha \Lambda^z\). alpha = 1 intervention, alpha < 1 attenuates process alpha > 1 intensifies . calibrate() calibrated intervention: intensity process exposure scaled alpha brings exposure value given toward. target composite parameter, whose standard error accounts alpha estimated. calibration rules : level(theta): exposure equals theta. absolute_change(delta): exposure delta plus value without intervention. relative_change(rho): exposure rho times value without intervention.

code: # Fixed intensity scalings. Halve the intensity of z, remove z altogether, # or double it: scale_intensity(z = 0.5) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(z = 0.5) scale_intensity(z = 0) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(z = 0) scale_intensity(z = 2) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(z = 2)  # A time-varying scaling: halve the intensity of z before time 0.5 only. scale_intensity(z = ~ ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(z = ~ifelse(time < 0.5, 0.5, 1))  # A scaling that depends on a baseline covariate: halve it only for # individuals with L0 > 0. scale_intensity(z = ~ ifelse(L0 > 0, 0.5, 1)) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(z = ~ifelse(L0 > 0, 0.5, 1))  # Several processes at once: scale_intensity(z = 0.5, death = 0.8) #> Intervention: scale_intensity(z = 0.5, death = 0.8)  # Calibrated interventions, scaling the intensity of z so that its risk # equals 0.1, falls by 0.05, or falls to 80% of its value without # intervention: calibrate(risk(z), level(0.1)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(z), level(0.1)) calibrate(risk(z), absolute_change(-0.05)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(z), absolute_change(-0.05)) calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(0.8)) #> Intervention: calibrate(risk(z), relative_change(0.8))  # Use them in tmle_estimate(): fit <- fit_initial(   illness_death,   models = list(     hazard_model(z ~ L0, limit = 1),     death ~ L0 + z,     censoring ~ L0   ),   tau = 1 ) tmle_estimate(fit, risk(death), scale_intensity(z = ~ ifelse(L0 > 0, 0.5, 1))) #> TMLE estimate of risk(death) #> under scale_intensity(z = ~ifelse(L0 > 0, 0.5, 1)) #>  #>    target  estimate        se     lower     upper #>    <char>     <num>     <num>     <num>     <num> #> 1:  death 0.3159039 0.0390286 0.2394092 0.3923985 #>  #> Initial estimate: 0.3159;
